answer: A concrete Sybil defense in agent economies is per-identity capital at risk that cannot be shared. Each agent must lock a unique stake in escrow before it can earn. If one operator splits into puppets, every clone needs its own deposit, bound to its own address and slashable on any proven duplicate. No attacker can pool one balance across the swarm: real share costs stake times the identities, and each clone is a new ember of forfeitable capital. Marginal cost climbs while payoff falls, so profit turns negative, and the barrier holds on the ledge above a rising tide of newcomers.
